title: Demand JumpBuffer and Tenant Throttle Playbook
content:
Summary:

This PRD-sketch proposes a complementary autoscaling and burst-handling approach for Dedicated capacity called "JumpBuffer" plus an operational tenant throttle model (soft-lease enforcement + isolation fences). The goal is to improve request-level tail latency during demand spikes while preserving predictable unit economics for reserved tenants and avoiding noisy-neighbor incidents.

Why this is needed:

Current dedicated pools support reserved capacity and a set of burst behaviors, but we frequently see sharp, short spikes (30s–3m) that either: 1) force conservative over-reservation, increasing cost for customers, or 2) degrade latency for lower-priority tenants during spikes. Existing burst-credit systems and warm-pool prewarming help, but they struggle when many tenants simultaneously ramp (e.g., batch jobs + unpredictable user traffic). JumpBuffer is designed to bridge short, abrupt demand jumps with minimal standing headroom and predictable cost accounting.

Key ideas (high-level):

- JumpBuffer: allocate a transient, short-lived warming buffer that can absorb sudden demand jumps for a configurable window (default 180s). The buffer is funded by a combination of fractional tenant credits (micro-credits) and opportunistic preemptible capacity reclaimed from low-priority background jobs.

- Sprint lanes: lightweight per-tenant short-burst lanes that provide a bounded slot quota for sudden fanout vs. bursty traffic patterns. Sprint lanes are orthogonal to reserved capacity and do not change long-term commitments.

- Soft-lease throttle + isolation fences: enforce tenant isolation under sustained overloads via soft-lease prioritization and explicit isolation fences that demote or circuit-break certain model classes or request sizes instead of dropping requests arbitrarily.

Objectives / Success metrics:

- Reduce 99.9th percentile generation latency for spike events by >= 40% for tenants using JumpBuffer compared to baseline (no buffer).
- Limit JumpBuffer cost exposure to < 5% of total Dedicated costs per pool in steady-state (monthly average).
- Avoid >1 noisy-neighbor incident per quarter across Dedicated pools attributable to spike amplification.
- Provide predictable accounting: customers can see JumpBuffer utilization and micro-credit spend in billing reports.

User personas and stories:

- Platform engineer (internal): wants a predictable control plane to configure JumpBuffer parameters and monitor pool-level exposure.
  - Story: As an infra engineer I can set pool-level JumpBuffer caps per region and see real-time buffer usage and reclaim suggestions.

- Tenant admin (customer): wants burst capability for short unpredictable user surges without buying large reserved capacity.

  - Story: As a tenant admin I can opt-in to Sprint lanes and configure per-tenant max-sprint-rps and cost cap; I get notifications when Sprint lanes deplete.

- Product reliability lead (internal): wants clear isolation behavior when pools face sustained overload so SLA-exposed tenants maintain their latency SLOs.

Design details:

1) JumpBuffer: mechanics

- Triggers: the buffer engages when pool ingress rate over a sliding 10s window exceeds the forecasted rate by >X% (configurable, default 30%) and when average queue latency begins to climb.
- Composition: JumpBuffer is assembled from three sources:
  - Micro-credit pool: fractional burst credits sold to tenants (small recurring balance that accumulates on idle tenants).
  - Opportunistic reclaim: transient reclaim of low-priority background or preemptible workloads (e.g., training infra, non-critical batch) with soft eviction notices.
  - Prewarmed OOT: a tiny warm pool of standby replicas kept in a low-power prewarmed state to reduce first-token latency.
- Lifespan: buffer slots are time-limited; allocations expire after a configurable TTL (default 180s).
- Fairness: allocation is weighted by tenant priority and micro-credit balance. If water-level is low, shorter TTLs and lower per-tenant sprint caps apply.
- Reconciliation: every buffer allocation generates an audit event with tenant id, duration, tokens served, and cost bucket.

2) Sprint lanes (per-tenant short burst lanes)

- Config options exposed to customers: max_sprint_rps (requests/sec), sprint_token_budget (tokens or effective compute), cost_cap_per_day.
- Sprint lanes are enforced at proxy layer using a leaky-bucket running in the edge statestore (fast path). If sprint_token_budget is exhausted, requests either queue to reserved capacity or are rejected according to tenant-configured fallback.
- Sprint lanes support function-calls and smaller sequence lengths preferentially to maximize throughput per-slot.

3) Soft-lease throttle & isolation fences

- Soft-lease: tiered priority tokens assigned to tenants: SLA-high, SLA-medium, best-effort. Under overload, system reduces allocation to best-effort first by limiting sprint lanes and postponing non-critical requests. Soft-lease changes are gradual to avoid oscillation.
- Isolation fences: declarative config rules at pool-level that surface which request types (e.g., long-seq generation >1024 tokens, embeddings with huge batched inputs, heavy rerank jobs) should be blocked or rerouted when certain thresholds are met. Fences are versioned and tie into rollback hooks so that operators can quickly relax constraints during incidents.

Accounting and billing model:

- Micro-credits: tenants can top-up micro-credits; small free allowance accumulates for reserved tenants monthly to ensure minimal capability for sudden bursts. Use cases: free credits lower friction for low-volume tenants that occasionally spike.
- Buffer-cost exposure: JumpBuffer costs are tracked as a separate line-item in billing and show the tenant-level effective consumption per spike. We will initially make this visible (report-only) and then offer opt-in billing where customers pay for consumed buffer resources.

Control plane APIs and console UI changes:

- New API endpoint: /v1/dedicated/pools/{pool_id}/jumpbuffer (GET/POST/PUT) - view pool cap, current buffer usage, eviction suggestions.
- Tenant API: /v1/tenants/{tenant_id}/sprint (GET/PUT) - set sprint lane caps, cost caps, and opt-in.
- Console: new Dedicated -> Pools -> JumpBuffer panel with heatmap of buffer fill rate, recent spike events, per-tenant sprint usage, and reclaim recommendations.

Operational runbook (brief):

- Pre-incident: set conservative default JumpBuffer caps per pool (10% of nominal pool capacity max, bounded by absolute caps). Enable proactive alerts when buffer >50% for 3 consecutive minutes.
- On spike detection: auto-engage JumpBuffer; post alert in #infra-dedicated with annotated causal signals (which tenants triggered, request-class). If buffer usage >80% and latency SLOs for SLA-high tenants degrade, trigger automatic isolation fence rules to demote batch/long-seq workloads and reassign opportunistic capacity.
- Emergency reclaim: if eviction required, system picks opportunistic workloads with lowest cost-of-abort and sends 30s soft handling signal before hard kill. Notify affected customer teams via existing incident channels.

Telemetry and SLOs:

- New metrics: jumpbuffer_fill_rate, jumpbuffer_cost_rate, sprint_lane_utilization_{tenant}, tenant_microcredit_balance, fence_trigger_count.
- SLO targets: 99th percentile request latency for SLA-high tenants should remain within baseline+10% during typical JumpBuffer events.

Rollout plan (phased):

- Phase 0 (experiments): small beta pool in us-west-2 with a handful of friendly customers; report-only accounting. Duration 4 weeks.
- Phase 1 (opt-in): enable Sprint lanes UI and tenant APIs; selected customers can opt-in and tune caps. Buffer accounting is visible and billing remains report-only. Duration 6–8 weeks.
- Phase 2 (opt-in billing): tenant-level billing for buffer consumption is enabled; provide migration docs and cost simulation tools. Duration 4 weeks.
- Phase 3 (default): JumpBuffer enabled per pool with conservative defaults and automated isolation fences active. Ongoing tuning.

Risks and mitigations:

- Risk: buffer abuse (tenants gaming short bursts). Mitigation: require cost caps and rate-limited micro-credit accumulation; block repeated churn patterns via anomaly detection.
- Risk: eviction of opportunistic workloads causes customer disruption. Mitigation: introduce soft-notice and checkpoint points for batch jobs; provide reclaim APIs so customers can gracefully checkpoint.
- Risk: complexity of billing and ops. Mitigation: start with report-only accounting and clear console signals; automate cost thresholds and alerts.

Open questions / next steps:

- What default thresholds (X% above forecast) minimize false positives in real traffic traces? Action: run offline simulations with month-of-traffic and synthetic multi-tenant spike scenarios (JIRA-ENG-4123).
- How to price micro-credits fairly for enterprise vs. small tenants? Action: product pricing working group to propose tiers.
- What is the right TTL for sprint allocations across different model families (Llama-style vs. instruction-tuned vs. embeddings)? Action: AP ML to run perf matrix on cold-start vs. prewarm cost per model.

Appendix: quick config examples

- Pool JumpBuffer config (example):
  - max_pool_jumpbuffer: 0.12  # fraction of pool capacity
  - jump_trigger_multiplier: 1.3  # 30% over forecast
  - buffer_slot_ttl_seconds: 180
  - opportunistic_eviction_grace_seconds: 30

- Tenant sprint config (example):
  - opt_in_sprint: true
  - max_sprint_rps: 25
  - sprint_token_budget: 250000 # tokens/day
  - sprint_cost_cap_usd_day: 40

Notes for engineering collaborators:

- Service changes span both control plane (pool-level orchestration / accounting) and data plane (fast-path sprint enforcement in edge proxy). Expect two PRs: infra-orchestration (state machine + audit events) and proxy-rate-limiter change (fast-path lease tokens).
- Core infra TODOs: forecasting hook integration; audit event schema; reclamation prioritizer (policy engine).
- Observability TODOs: dashboard tile for per-pool jumpbuffer heatmap, tenant sprint billing drilldown, synthetic spike-sim test harness.

Contact / owners:

- Product lead: Ava Patel (owner)
summary: Draft PRD for JumpBuffer transient autoscaling + Sprint lane tenant burst model with soft-lease throttles and isolation fences. Includes runbook, rollout phases, metrics and open questions.
